az_new_wave_wall.blurb: A steep, mostly sport wall among the roadside cliffs at Windy Point on Mount Lemmon, high above Tucson. The face leans back only slightly but steadily, and the climbing is power-oriented on small crimps. Of eleven routes, ten are bolted and one needs gear. Most are hard: the bulk sit around 5.12, with a pair at 5.11 and a couple of easier lines at 5.7 and 5.8 for warming up. The wall keeps its morning shade, which helps in warmer months. The base is only a short scramble from the pullouts, so it suits a quick session.
az_new_wave_wall.parking_note: Park at the large Windy Point vista lot or at a Catalina Highway pullout a little below it. The wall is a short walk from there.

az_spectrum_wall.blurb: A compact sport wall of eleven routes on the Upper Highway stretch of Mount Lemmon, perched at roughly 7,500 feet above the upper end of Sabino Canyon. The stone is good quality though rough on fingertips. Grades start around 5.10 and cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with a few harder lines pushing well beyond that, so it is a place for strong intermediates and up rather than beginners. The wall faces west, giving shade in the morning and sun later in the day. Reaching it takes a long, route-finding-heavy hike, and the crag is quiet and scenic.

az_tall_wall.blurb: A low-angle slab of bolted face climbing in the Outcroppings, mid-mountain on Mount Lemmon at about 7,300 feet. All eleven routes are sport, and most are long, around 195 feet, with a lower-off at mid-height so they can be split into two pitches or climbed as one. Grades are friendly: mostly 5.8 with a few easier lines and one at 5.10. The south-facing wall warms up well, making it a pleasant choice from fall through spring and cool early mornings in summer. Bring a 60 m rope and plenty of quickdraws.
az_tall_wall.parking_note: Take the Mount Lemmon Highway to about mile marker 19.4, just before the ranger station, and turn left onto Organization Ridge Road. The Palisades Trailhead lot is roughly 0.3 miles up this road.
az_tall_wall.approach: From the lot, walk a short way along the road, then take the path on the left and climb past a black stump, following cairns to a large cairn. Continue to the top of Cave Wall and Tall Wall, then drop right over slabs and a short steep path to the base.

az_incinerated_ridge.blurb: A sport wall of eleven bolted face climbs in the Outcroppings, mid-mountain on Mount Lemmon at roughly 7,250 feet. Lines are easiest toward the right end and grow steadily harder heading left. Grades run from about 5.6 through 5.10, with the largest share around 5.7, so it works well for newer leaders and moderate cragging days. Some trees shade the left side. It sits next to Tall Wall and Cave Wall, so a day here can easily combine two or three walls.
az_incinerated_ridge.parking_note: Take the Mount Lemmon Highway to about mile marker 19.4, just before the ranger station, and turn left onto Organization Ridge Road. The Palisades Trailhead lot is roughly 0.3 miles up this road.
az_incinerated_ridge.approach: From the lot, walk a short way along the road, then take the path on the left and climb past a black stump, following cairns to a large cairn. Continue toward the top of Cave Wall and Tall Wall, then angle right and down the slabs to the wall.

az_towers_the_2.blurb: A shadowy recess where Munchkin Wall ends on the left, in Mount Lemmon's Munchkinland, with lines climbing either side of the cleft. All eleven routes are sport, and the range is wide and beginner-friendly: from about 5.4 up to 5.11, with most lines between 5.7 and 5.10, and some of the easier ones surprisingly long. The northwest-facing walls stay shaded until about midday, so it stays comfortable on warm days. It is the first group of routes reached on the switchbacks, and it can be linked with the neighbouring wall in one outing.
az_towers_the_2.parking_note: Drive to the end of Rose Canyon Road and use one of the large lots near the lake.
az_towers_the_2.approach: Start on the trail behind the old snack bar, heading to the ridgeline and a clearing, then turn right and follow the switchbacks downhill. The Towers is the first group of routes you reach.

az_2_king.blurb: A lower-elevation Mount Lemmon sector in the Chessman Area, close to the Catalina Highway at roughly 5,200 feet. Ten of the eleven routes are bolted and one is trad, spanning 5.10 into the 5.12s with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. It is the shadiest wall in the area, with sun not arriving until mid-afternoon, which makes it a good choice when other nearby cliffs are baking. The walk in is a steep, rocky drainage with a little scrambling. Expect moderate-to-hard sport climbing rather than easy mileage.
az_2_king.approach: Hike straight up the rocky drainage from the road for about 15 minutes, with some scrambling. At the fork near the cliff, take the uphill left branch.

az_wailing_wall_2.blurb: A short limestone amphitheater among the Bright Angel Walls on the Grand Canyon's South Rim, just below the rim road. The routes are brief, a mix of bolted lines, gear climbs and one top-rope, with fossil-studded rock and some anchors on trees. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.10, with several at 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate terrain. It makes a pleasant spot for a few hours of cragging with canyon views.
